title: Lentil and Goat's Cheese Salad
subtitle: Puy lentils with creamy goat's cheese and a sharp mustardy dressing
excerpt: Puy lentils dressed warm in a Dijon vinaigrette, topped with crumbled goat's cheese, walnuts and a few salad leaves. A French bistro classic that works as a starter or a light lunch.
sourceNotes: Lentil salad with goat's cheese is a fixture of the French bistro repertoire, particularly in the Loire valley where both Puy lentils (from Le Puy-en-Velay) and goat's cheese have strong regional associations. Salade aux lentilles avec fromage de chevre became well known in British cooking through the influence of Elizabeth David, and later through the expansion of the bistro format in London from the 1990s onward.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the lentils and dress them a day ahead; add goat's cheese and walnuts just before serving.

content.text: Lentil and goat's cheese salad works because the warm lentils absorb the mustardy vinaigrette, and the creamy, acidic goat's cheese cuts through the earthiness of the grain. Dress the lentils while they are still warm from cooking. Cold lentils do not absorb dressing and the salad will taste flat. Puy lentils are the best choice: they hold their shape after cooking, where red or orange lentils collapse.

Rinse {{puy-lentils}} of Puy lentils and place in a saucepan. Cover with cold water by about 5 cm. Do not salt yet: salt toughens the skins of lentils during cooking. Bring to the boil, reduce the heat and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until just tender but still holding their shape. Drain, then season with salt and toss with the red onion.

Whisk together {{white-wine-vinegar}} of white wine vinegar, {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of black pepper. Pour the dressing over the warm lentils and toss to coat. Leave to rest for 5 minutes.

Tip the dressed lentils onto spinach or watercress leaves if using. Scatter over the {{goats-cheese}} of crumbled goat's cheese, {{walnuts}} of walnuts and chopped parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.fix: Check from 18 minutes. Puy lentils should have a slight bite when they are done; they will continue softening slightly from residual heat after draining.

items.cause: Lentils not salted after cooking, or dressed cold.
items.fix: Always dress lentils while warm. Season assertively with salt after draining; unsalted lentils taste flat regardless of how good the dressing is.

content.text: This salad comes from the French bistro tradition, where lentilles du Puy have been a kitchen staple since the lentil was awarded an AOC (appellation d'origine controlee) designation in 1996. The pairing with goat's cheese is characteristically French: the Loire valley produces both excellent Puy lentils (from the Auvergne, nearby) and the great fresh chevre of the region. In Britain the dish is now firmly embedded in cafe lunch culture.
